title: Prompt Slot Allocator and Backfill Protocol (scratch)
body:
Quick brain-dump / working spec for a lightweight per-request "prompt-slot" allocator that helps hosting tier(s) handle bursty tenant traffic (interactive chat, embed spikes) while enabling controlled backfill/warmup of model KV/LLM contexts. Intended for early sketch — tradeoffs, gotchas, and API shapes included.

Goal summary:
- Allow ingress to request ephemeral "slots" for prompt processing with constraints (max-latency, cost-target, can-backfill) so scheduler can place requests into burst lanes or slow backfill lanes.
- Support a fast path for low-latency priority slots and a backfill path that can accept deferred/queueable prompts that tolerate longer latency (e.g., background summarization, async reruns).
- Provide consumer-configurable hints and server-side decisions (prewarm, reuse, QoS downgrade) without leaking infra details.

Design primitives (v0):
- SlotRequest (client-facing hint object)
  - id: client-generated id (optional)
  - tenant_id: derived from API key
  - priority_hint: p0..p4 (p0 highest)
  - latency_budget_ms: int (soft)
  - cost_target_usd_per_1k_tokens: float (optional)
  - can_backfill: bool (if true, server may defer and run on backfill lane)
  - warmup_needed: enum {none, kv_warm, full_model_warm} (hint)
  - preferred_model_variants: [string] (ordered list)

- SlotResponse (server)
  - slot_token: string (short-lived)
  - lane: {fast, warmup, backfill, delayed} (which lane assigned)
  - estimated_start_ms: int (approx)
  - max_wait_ms: int (if queued)
  - accepted_model_variant: string
  - prewarm_actions: [string] (e.g., "kv_load", "kv_prefetch:prefix_hash")
  - fallback_reason: string (optional)
body_continued:
(continued notes)

API shapes (HTTP+JSON)
- POST /v1/slots/request  
  payload: SlotRequest JSON
  response: SlotResponse JSON or 202 Accepted with slot_token when queued

- GET /v1/slots/status?slot_token=...  -> {status: pending|allocated|running|cancelled, lane, eta_ms, assigned_node}

- POST /v1/slots/cancel {slot_token}  -> 200/204

Operational semantics (sketch):
- Ingress path first attempts to allocate fast slots with idle capacity. If tenant has active reserved capacity, prioritize their fast lane.
- If no fast capacity, the allocator can: 1) queue into backfill (if can_backfill), 2) downgrade QoS and return a fast slot but with model_variant downgraded, or 3) return an immediate rejection.
- Backfill lane semantics: ordered FIFO per-tenant with burst windows and credit accounting. Backfill may run on cheaper hardware or preemptible nodes. Backfill jobs must be idempotent-safe.

Slot lifecycle state machine (notes):
- requested -> allocated (slot_token issued) OR queued -> prewarm -> running -> completed | cancelled | failed
- queued -> cancelled if wait exceeded max_wait_ms or tenant cancels

Telemetry and cost attribution:
- Emit per-slot events: slot.requested, slot.allocated, slot.prewarm.start/finish, slot.run.start/finish, slot.cancelled, slot.fallback
- Attach labels: tenant_id, route, model_variant, lane, node_type (preemptible|reserved|gpu_tier), cost_estimate_tokens, latency_budget_ms

Internal scheduler heuristics (very rough):
- Maintain per-tenant moving window credits (burst budget) — refill rate from plan (reserved RPS or token commit)
- Fast lane consumes credits; if short, allow short burst from global pool up to tenant max_burst_pct
- Backfill consumes zero-burst credits but counts against daily token quota; scheduled on low-cost pools first
- Prewarm: if warmup_needed == kv_warm, schedule an async KV load (prefetch based on key prefix heuristics). If warmup_needed == full_model_warm, schedule a short-duration model spin-up. Prewarming should return a small readiness token included in slot_response.prewarm_actions.

Example JSON request/response (concrete):
Request:
{
  "id": "tmp-4587",
  "tenant_id": "t_acme",
  "priority_hint": "p1",
  "latency_budget_ms": 150,
  "cost_target_usd_per_1k_tokens": 0.60,
  "can_backfill": true,
  "warmup_needed": "kv_warm",
  "preferred_model_variants": ["gptx-3.2q", "gptx-3.2q-8bit"]
}

Possible responses:
Immediate fast slot:
{
  "slot_token": "slt_xx123",
  "lane": "fast",
  "estimated_start_ms": 40,
  "max_wait_ms": 120,
  "accepted_model_variant": "gptx-3.2q",
  "prewarm_actions": []
}

Queued backfill (202):
HTTP 202
{
  "slot_token": "slt_xxQ",
  "lane": "backfill",
  "estimated_start_ms": 12000,
  "max_wait_ms": 600000,
  "accepted_model_variant": "gptx-3.2q-8bit",
  "prewarm_actions": ["kv_prefetch:user-prefix-9012"]
}

Edge cases / open questions (TODO):
- How to handle multi-call sessions that require KV warm across subsequent prompts? Attach persistent slot_token across session, or have explicit slot extend API? Risk: slot hoarding.
- Security: slot_token is short-lived but may be abused; bind to api-key + timestamp signature.
- Billing: do we bill queued/backfill tokens at request time or execution time? Prefer execution time. Need to surface expected cost to client early.
- Prewarm cost amortization: if we prewarm and job cancelled, who pays? Possibly charge a small prewarm fee or deduct from tenant burst credits.
- Backfill privacy: using cheaper pools may have different data isolation constraints (private vs shared). Need tenant opt-out.

Implementation concerns / quick plan:
- Minimal PoC: implement slot service as separate microservice that handles socket for slot token issuance. It communicates with runtime scheduler via small gRPC surface (AllocateSlot, PollSlotStatus, ReleaseSlot). Keep it stateless with Redis for queues and per-tenant credit ledger.
- Integrate with existing telemetry pipeline (span attributes) and billing surface.
- Start without prewarm (warmup_needed ignored) to validate API and queueing.

Non-functional goals and SLOs:
- Fast lane allocation latency < 50ms 90th pct under normal load
- Queue time estimate accuracy within +/- 20% median
- Backfill completion within declared max_wait_ms 95% when not overloaded

Sketch ascii diagram:
  client ---> ingress (API & auth) ---> slot-service (decides lane) ---> scheduler ---> runtime-pool {fast-nodes, backfill-nodes}
                 |                                       ^                       |                  
                 +---> /v1/slots/status polls ------------+                       +--> prewarm-queue

Notes to self:
- Keep API minimal. We don't want developers to manage warmup intricacies; provide hints and let server decide.
- Must tie into product: expose tenant controls in console for prefer-backfill, backfill-allowed, prewarm-budget.

Next steps:
- Sync with scheduler folks (Marco) to align per-tenant credit ledger schema (ENG-8213).
- PoC slot-service: allocate tokens, simple queue on Redis, basic telemetry. 2-week spike.
- UX: design console toggles and per-route defaults.

Random thoughts:
- Could use slot_token as a way to checkpoint prewarm state across retries: client retries with same slot_token within x seconds to reuse prewarm result. Could help latency for clients with flaky networks.
- Consider a two-tier slot_token: ephemeral short token for immediate run, long-lived reservation token for session-affiliated workloads (charge higher).

End of scratchpad.
